title: Climate Change
full_title: Climate Change: Evidence, Impacts and Responses
tagline: Observed change, detection and attribution, emissions and carbon budgets, projections, extremes, sea-level rise, tipping points, impacts, mitigation and adaptation
summary: This course examines what is known about human-caused climate change and how it is known. It covers the observed changes across the climate system, detection and attribution, greenhouse-gas emissions and carbon budgets, projections of future climate and extremes, sea-level rise and tipping points, impacts on ecosystems and people, and the evidence on options for mitigation and adaptation — with the uncertainty ranges of the assessed literature, and keeping physical science separate from policy choices.

chapters.title: Observed changes in the climate system
chapters.summary: The instrumental temperature record, ocean heat content, ice, sea level and other indicators, and how they are measured.

chapters.title: Detection and attribution
chapters.summary: Fingerprints of different causes, the attribution of the observed warming, and the attribution of individual extreme events.

chapters.title: Emissions and carbon budgets
chapters.summary: The sources of greenhouse gases, the near-linear relation between cumulative carbon dioxide emissions and warming, and remaining carbon budgets.

chapters.title: Projections of future climate
chapters.summary: Scenarios and global warming levels, and projected changes in temperature, precipitation and circulation.

chapters.title: Extremes in a warming world
chapters.summary: Observed and projected changes in heatwaves, heavy precipitation, droughts and tropical cyclones.

chapters.title: Sea-level rise
chapters.summary: Contributions from ocean warming, glaciers and ice sheets, projections, and the long-term commitment to rising seas.

chapters.title: Tipping points and irreversibility
chapters.summary: Ice sheets, the overturning circulation, permafrost and forests: thresholds, abrupt change and the strength of the evidence.

chapters.title: Impacts on ecosystems and people
chapters.summary: Effects on ecosystems, water, food, health and settlements, and how risk depends on exposure and vulnerability.

chapters.title: Mitigation and adaptation
chapters.summary: The evidence on options to reduce emissions, remove carbon dioxide and adapt, with their costs, limits and trade-offs as assessed by the IPCC.
